title: AEP expects electric sales to jump 8.6% annually over 3 years
summary: American Electric Power (AEP) projects an 8.6% annual increase in retail electric sales over the next three years, driven primarily by the growth of new data centers and industrial facilities. This demand may necessitate an additional $10 billion investment in infrastructure beyond their current capital plan, and AEP is exploring small modular reactors in Indiana and Virginia while using fuel cells to support current data center expansions. The utility also reported a significant jump in 2024 earnings.

title: Toy Companies are Coming Together at the TOTY® Awards to Deliver Play to Children in Need
summary: The 25th Toy of the Year (TOTY) Awards, scheduled for February 28, is bringing together toy companies to support The Toy Foundation (TTF). This gala serves as a crucial fundraiser for TTF to continue its mission of delivering toys and funding play-focused grants to children in need. Event sponsors like Amazon, Hasbro, and Mattel are helping TTF provide comfort and joy to millions of children, with various opportunities available for individuals and companies to contribute.

title: FedEx, UPS seek to prove they can thrive in busiest holiday rush
summary: FedEx and UPS are facing a critical test to prove they can maintain profitability during the busiest holiday shipping season, following a surge in demand due to the coronavirus pandemic. Both companies have implemented aggressive peak-season fees and are competing with Amazon for seasonal drivers, as they aim to demonstrate their ability to extract more profit from residential deliveries while avoiding capacity crunches. This challenge comes after significant investments in infrastructure and a recent increase in their stock performance.

title: Gorilla Technology Secures Multi-Billion Dollar Internet of Forests Contract with One Amazon | GRRR Stock News
summary: Gorilla Technology Group (NASDAQ: GRRR) has secured a multi-billion dollar, multi-year contract with ONE AMAZON to create the world's first Internet of Forests (IoF) in the Amazon rainforest. This initiative involves deploying environmental biodegradable sensors, satellite imagery, drone surveillance, and AI algorithms to monitor the ecosystem in real-time. Goldman Sachs is also involved, developing a tradable financial platform to convert natural capital into digital assets, aiming to make the Amazon an investable asset through nature-backed securities and blockchain tokens.

title: Adeia Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Financial Results
summary: Adeia announced strong financial results for Q4 and Full Year 2024, achieving record post-separation revenue and cash from operations and signing 10 deals in Q4, including new strategic agreements with Amazon, Canon, and a luxury retailer. The company also paid down $50 million in debt and repurchased $20 million of common stock, while growing its patent portfolio by 12% to over 12,000 assets. Adeia provided a positive financial outlook for full year 2025, projecting revenue between $390.0 million and $430.0 million.

title: The Top 3 Stocks that Can Become the Next Amazon
summary: This article identifies three stocks – Sea Limited (SE), MercadoLibre (MELI), and Alibaba (BABA) – as having the potential to become regional equivalents of Amazon. It highlights Sea Limited's dominance in Southeast Asian e-commerce through Shopee, MercadoLibre's comprehensive e-commerce and digital payments platform in Latin America, and Alibaba's significant presence in China with strong growth potential and an undervalued stock. The piece emphasizes the expanding global e-commerce and digital payments markets as a growth driver for these companies.

title: Oz pledges to divest from HCA Healthcare and UnitedHealth if confirmed
summary: Mehmet Oz, nominated to lead the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, has committed to divesting his investments in various healthcare companies, including HCA Healthcare and United Health Group, if confirmed. These divestments would occur within 90 days of his confirmation. He also plans to resign from advisory roles and sell shares in other healthcare ventures, while retaining ownership in his cattle ranch and Turkish real estate.

title: Retail Insights® 2025 Retail Universe for U.S. Premium Natural, Organic Foods, Supplements & Personal Care
summary: In 2024, the U.S. natural organic products market saw significant growth, adding $7.137 billion in sales to reach $110.75 billion, outpacing conventional grocery channels. Supernaturals like Whole Foods and Sprouts maintained their lead, while compact grocers and club stores experienced the highest percentage growth in natural organic sales. The report details the performance of eight retail channels, highlighting the increasing market share and productivity of natural organic products.

title: Does Plug Power Stock Have Any Power to Rally?
summary: Plug Power (PLUG) stock, currently trading at $1.77 after peaking at $75.49 in January 2021, is analyzed for a potential rally. Despite significant challenges in scaling hydrogen infrastructure, such as high costs and regulatory uncertainty, the company's strong partnerships and expansion into hydrogen production suggest long-term potential. Technical analysis shows a bullish divergence in momentum and a potential double bottom pattern, suggesting a possible reversal if it closes above $1.85.

title: ST launches SiPho and next-gen BiCMOS technologies for higher-performing cloud optical interconnect in data centers and AI clusters
summary: STMicroelectronics has announced new silicon photonics (SiPho) and BiCMOS technologies aimed at improving optical interconnect performance in data centers and AI clusters. These technologies, set to ramp up from late 2025 for 800Gb/s and 1.6Tb/s optical modules, will integrate multiple complex components onto a single chip and offer ultra-high-speed, low-power connectivity. AWS is collaborating with STMicroelectronics on the PIC100 SiPho technology, highlighting the industry's need for advanced solutions to meet growing AI demands.

title: STMicroelectronics unveils new data center photonics chip for AI workload interconnects
summary: STMicroelectronics has introduced the PIC100, a new data center photonics chip designed in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to support 800Gbps and 1.6Tbps optical interconnects for AI workloads. This chip, the first in STMicroelectronics' new PIC product family, combines silicon photonics and BiCMOS technologies on a 300mm silicon platform. It aims to provide ultra-high speed and low-power optical technology, essential for sustainable AI growth, and will be manufactured in France.

title: This £1.99 product is the key to getting oil out of a carpet — no expensive carpet cleaner required
summary: Bicarbonate of soda, a common and inexpensive product, is highlighted as the most effective solution for removing oil stains from carpets. The article provides a step-by-step guide, emphasizing the importance of quickly scooping up excess oil, blotting, applying bicarbonate of soda, vacuuming, and, if necessary, using washing-up liquid. It also advises on post-cleaning carpet care and cautions against using WD-40 or relying solely on vinegar.

title: Adobe Announces General Availability of Real-Time CDP Collaboration for Brands to Jointly Drive Ad Performance in a Privacy-First Landscape
summary: Adobe has announced the general availability of its Real-Time CDP Collaboration in the U.S., a new solution designed to help advertisers and publishers navigate the evolving privacy-first advertising landscape. This platform allows brands to securely collaborate on first-party data to identify high-value audiences and activate personalized ad campaigns without sharing directly identifiable customer data. Partners like Warner Bros. Discovery are already leveraging this tool to enhance ad performance and audience targeting.

title: Prologis CEO Hamid Moghadam to retire next year
summary: Hamid Moghadam, co-founder and CEO of Prologis, plans to retire on January 1, 2026, after more than four decades with the company and its predecessor. Dan Letter, current president, will succeed him as CEO, while Moghadam will transition to executive chairman. This succession plan has been in the works for over two years, with Letter having joined AMB in 2004 and becoming president of Prologis in January 2023.

title: KKR’s Sale of Logistics Provider Goodpack Attracts Investors
summary: KKR & Co.'s attempt to sell its logistics services provider Goodpack has drawn interest from major investment firms including Apollo Global Management Inc., I Squared Capital, and Stonepeak Partners. Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. and Chinese firms like China Merchants Group Ltd. also show preliminary interest. A potential sale could value Goodpack at about $1.5 billion, though discussions are in early stages and may not lead to a transaction.

title: Rivian expands commercial van sales, ending Amazon exclusivity
summary: Rivian has expanded its commercial electric van sales to all U.S. businesses, ending its exclusivity agreement with Amazon that concluded in November 2023. This strategic move aims to boost Rivian's bottom line as it prepares to launch a more affordable SUV next year. Meanwhile, electric truck maker Nikola has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, seeking a buyer for its entire business after failing to secure capital, while other related news includes funding for EV charging infrastructure and continued electric truck battery manufacturing ventures.

title: Wellgistics Health (NASDAQ:WGRX) IPO: Revolutionizing Pharmacy Care for a Patient-Centric Future
summary: Wellgistics Health (NASDAQ:WGRX) is launching its IPO at $4.50, poised to disrupt the healthcare landscape with a patient-centric approach to pharmacy care. The company aims to address inefficiencies in the pharmacy ecosystem through software solutions, an online pharmacy, and proprietary drug distribution, including formulations for GLP-1 and Long Covid. With an experienced management team and multiple revenue streams, WGRX presents a compelling investment opportunity despite a relatively thin float.

title: Sherwin-Williams Is a Sleeper of the 100,000% Return Club
summary: Sherwin-Williams (SHW) has quietly delivered massive returns for shareholders, achieving a 122,000% return since 1980. This success is attributed to its pervasive presence in the paint market, strategic acquisitions like Valspar, diligent cost-squeezing, and significant share buybacks. The company also maintains a modest but consistently growing dividend with a safe payout ratio, further contributing to its total shareholder return.

title: Costco chairman reveals surprising luxury items that are selling out
summary: Costco's chairman, Hamilton "Tony" James, highlighted that the retailer successfully sells a surprising range of luxury items, from Porsches to Rolex watches, Dom Perignon, and gold bars. He noted that despite a generally average-income customer base, the presence of affluent members with double the average income allows Costco to move high-end products rapidly due to their appreciation for good deals. James also mentioned the recent quick sale of gold bars, questioning whether affluent individuals or those wary of the economy are driving these purchases.

title: PLDT Expands International Capacity with Apricot Cable System
summary: PLDT, Inc. has completed the landing of the Apricot submarine cable system in Baler, Aurora, and Digos, Davao, significantly increasing its international data capacity by 33% to over 140 Tbps. This new 12,000-kilometer cable system enhances network resilience and supports the growing demand for digital services across the Asia Pacific and the U.S., strategically positioning the Philippines as a digital hub. The system's routing avoids earthquake-prone areas and establishes direct connections, making it a critical intra-Asia hub for OTT service providers and vital for supporting next-generation technologies.

title: Why Is Amazon Stock Down Today? AMZN Price Hits 2-Month Lows Amid High Price Predictions
summary: Amazon (AMZN) stock has fallen to two-month lows, currently at $216.58, despite strong Q4 2024 results, due to a Q1 2025 sales forecast below Wall Street expectations and concerns over a $100 billion spending plan for AWS and AI. Analysts remain bullish for the long term, with price targets ranging from $260-$280 for 2025 and a potential $3 trillion market cap by 2026, driven by growth in AWS, AI, and e-commerce despite short-term volatility and macroeconomic factors. The article provides a detailed analysis of Amazon's financial performance, technical indicators, and market factors influencing its stock price.

title: Earnings call transcript: Navitas Semiconductor Q4 2024 revenue miss hits stock
summary: Navitas Semiconductor reported its Q4 2024 earnings, with an EPS meeting expectations but revenue significantly missing forecasts ($18 million vs. $23.99 million). This shortfall led to a 16.95% after-hours stock drop. Despite this, the company maintains a strong cash position, anticipates a recovery starting in Q2 2025, and aims for positive EBITDA by 2026, driven by growth in data center, EV, and mobile markets.

title: Apple commits to 'largest ever' $500bn US investment
summary: Apple announced a multi-year plan to invest over $500 billion in the US and create 20,000 new jobs, with a focus on research, development, software, and AI. This commitment includes building a new manufacturing factory in Texas to support its AI system, Apple Intelligence, and expanding data centers across several states. The announcement comes after Apple CEO Tim Cook met with President Donald Trump, who has consistently pushed for increased domestic manufacturing.

title: Retail Traffic Is Carter’s Profitability Challenge
summary: Carter's Inc. experienced improved fourth-quarter results in 2024 due to strategic pricing adjustments; however, declining retail traffic to its stores remains a significant challenge for 2025 profitability. The company plans to open 250 new U.S. stores by 2027 and enhance product assortments and marketing to drive traffic and improve market share. Despite a dip in net income, Carter's wholesale business remains profitable, and new brand launches and product extensions are expected to fuel sales growth.

title: The Real World: How DePIN Bridges Crypto Back to Physical Systems
summary: This article explores Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks (DePINs) as a non-speculative application of blockchain technology, connecting crypto to physical systems like wireless connectivity and AI computing resources. It highlights Solana as the leading blockchain for DePINs due to its speed and cost-effectiveness, featuring examples like Helium, Render, and Grass. The piece emphasizes the benefits of DePINs, such as eliminating intermediaries and aligning incentives, which could significantly impact industries like internet connectivity, data storage, and AI hardware.

title: Work-from-home warning as more bosses drag staff back into the office: ‘Domino effect’
summary: A "domino effect" is leading more Australian employers to mandate full-time office work, with nearly two in five requiring five days a week in the office. This trend, driven by companies like Amazon and Dell, is increasing the average required office days and reducing remote work flexibility. Despite some employee pushback and demands for higher salaries to compensate for commuting costs, employers are banking on improved office environments and career development to entice staff back.

title: Number Sense: Cracking the code behind Sprouts’ striking success
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market has shown remarkable financial success, with significant increases in same-store sales and stock price, contrasting with other grocers. This growth is attributed to its strategy of targeting health-focused shoppers willing to pay higher prices, shifting to smaller, more profitable store formats, and effectively expanding its private label offerings. Originally underperforming, Sprouts has successfully pivoted to achieve strong financial returns and investor confidence.

title: 6 Essential E-commerce Marketing Metrics to Track
summary: This article highlights six essential e-commerce marketing metrics that businesses should track to ensure effective marketing efforts and sustained growth. It covers Conversion Rate, Customer Acquisition Cost, Returning Customer Rate, Average Order Value, Cart Abandonment Rate, and Return on Ad Spend. The piece also discusses how to determine which metrics matter, how often to check them, and practical ways to track and improve these KPIs using various tools and strategies.

title: Nvidia to report earnings amid infrastructure spending, DeepSeek concerns
summary: Nvidia is set to release its fourth-quarter earnings, capping off a remarkable year of growth driven by demand for its data center GPUs essential for AI. Despite its success, investors are cautious due to concerns about major customers potentially tightening capital expenditure and the emergence of more efficient AI models from startups like DeepSeek, which could reduce the need for extensive GPU infrastructure. CEO Jensen Huang is expected to address these concerns, emphasizing the continued need for GPUs in AI development and deployment, particularly for the inference phase.

title: QVCGA - QVC Group Inc Stock Price and Quote
summary: This article provides comprehensive stock information for QVC Group Inc (QVCGA), including its current price, financial metrics, and recent news. It details analyst ratings, insider transactions, and a timeline of corporate announcements, highlighting financial results, strategic moves like a reverse stock split, and management changes. The company operates through QxH, QVC International, and CBI segments, focusing on video and online commerce.

title: Investors Cautious on Nvidia Stock Before Earnings
summary: Nvidia (NVDA) stock sees investor caution ahead of its fourth-quarter earnings report, despite a historical trend of post-earnings gains. Concerns about China's AI advancements and potential slowing demand from customers have led to the stock sliding, with Wolfe Research calling the report a "make or break" moment. Options traders are pricing in a significant post-earnings move of 15.2%, higher than its average swing, while volatility expectations remain low.

title: Self-Service Payments Firm Cantaloupe Reportedly Weighs Sale
summary: Cantaloupe, a self-service payments technology and software company, is reportedly considering a sale or a go-private transaction. This comes as mergers and acquisitions in the digital payments space have seen robust activity for niche companies, with larger firms looking to bolster offerings and private equity increasing investments. Cantaloupe's CEO has previously discussed the challenges and potential for modernizing self-service payments to create frictionless consumer experiences.

summary: This article provides detailed information about the NEOS Nasdaq-100 Hedged Equity Income ETF (QQQH), including its current price, key statistics, overview, and expense ratios. title: After waiting with bated breath, Wall Street absorbs Nvidia's latest earnings
summary: Nvidia's latest earnings report reveals $39.3 billion in revenue, a 78% increase for the quarter ending in January, surpassing analyst expectations. The chipmaker's performance is crucial for Wall Street due to its significant market valuation and central role in the AI sector. Despite strong revenue, Nvidia's forward-looking statements signaled slowing profit-margin growth, and concerns about sustaining the rapid pace of AI investment and recent economic slowdowns have impacted its stock.

title: Is Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) the Best Magic Formula Stock for 2025?
summary: This article examines Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) in the context of Joel Greenblatt's "Magic Formula" investment strategy, which uses earnings yield and return on capital. While AMZN ranks 4th on a list of best magic formula stocks for 2025, the article notes the strategy's historical performance, potential risks, and Greenblatt's own fund's recent underperformance against the S&P 500. It also highlights an analyst's positive outlook for AWS's generative AI revenue growth.

title: Nokia gets EU nod for $2.3 bn Infinera buy, challenging Ciena and Huawei
summary: Nokia has received unconditional EU approval for its $2.3 billion acquisition of Infinera, a move expected to significantly bolster its position in the optical networking market. This acquisition will make Nokia the second-largest vendor globally, enhancing its ability to supply major tech companies and compete more effectively with Huawei and Ciena. Nokia anticipates achieving €200 million in operating profit synergies by 2027 and positive earnings per share contribution in the first year.

title: Veeva Adds Direct Data API to Veeva Vault Platform
summary: Veeva has launched a new Direct Data API for its Veeva Vault Platform, offering access to Vault data up to 100 times faster than traditional APIs without additional licensing fees. This API aims to facilitate AI applications, analytics, and system integrations through reliable, high-speed extraction of large datasets, with future connectors planned for major data platforms.

title: After Earnings, Is Walmart Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $58 per share for Walmart (WMT) and rates it as significantly overvalued following its fiscal first-quarter earnings report. Despite strong performance in key metrics like comparable sales and high-margin profit streams, underwhelming fiscal 2026 guidance led to a stock sell-off. Morningstar believes Walmart possesses a wide economic moat due to its brand, cost advantage, and extensive physical footprint, but faces risks from e-commerce competition.

title: Preliminary Results 2024
summary: WPP announced its preliminary results for 2024, showing strategic progress in margin and cash conversion despite top-line pressures. The company reported a headline operating profit of £1,707m with a 15.0% margin, driven by structural cost savings and AI investment. WPP is focusing on AI, data, and technology through WPP Open and expects LFL revenue less pass-through costs to be flat to -2% in 2025, with improvement in the second half of the year.

title: Pearson and AWS Announce Collaboration to Unlock AI-Powered Personalized Learning for Millions of People Globally
summary: Pearson and Amazon Web Services (AWS) are expanding their collaboration to accelerate AI-powered personalized learning for millions globally. Building on a 13-year partnership, Pearson will significantly increase its use of AWS cloud infrastructure and Amazon Bedrock to enhance and scale its higher education products, virtual schools, and English-language learning. This initiative aims to make learning more effective, efficient, and accessible, providing AI-powered tools for educators and enriching content experiences for learners.

title: NetApp misses Q3 expectations as deal slippage hits sales
summary: NetApp reported disappointing Q3 FY2025 results, missing revenue targets with a modest 2 percent year-over-year rise to $1.64 billion, attributed largely to deal slippage late in the quarter. CEO George Kurian acknowledged the "below our standards" performance and outlined steps to improve execution, despite experiencing growth in public cloud services and securing over 100 AI and data lake modernization deals. The company anticipates a rebound in Q4, but analysts maintain a cautious outlook.

title: Progyny projects slower revenue growth after losing Amazon
summary: Progyny, a fertility benefits company, anticipates slower revenue growth in 2025 due to losing Amazon, its largest client, which accounted for 12% of its previous year's revenue. Despite this, Progyny reported strong 2024 earnings of $1.2 billion and saw its stock significantly increase on Thursday. The company also highlighted potential positive implications from a recent Trump administration executive order aimed at bolstering access to IVF treatments.
